title: Κολοιὸς φυγάς
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 164. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Κολοιόν τις συλλαβὼν καὶ δήσας αὐτοῦ τὸν πόδα λινῷ κάλῳ τῷ ἑαυτοῦ παιδὶ ἔδωκεν.
sentences.tr: Koloion tis syllabōn kai dēsas autou ton poda linōi kalōi tōi heautou paidi edōken.
sentences.l: Someone, having caught a jackdaw and having tied its foot with a linen cord, gave it to his own child.
sentences.n: κάλως is properly a ship's rope; λινῷ κάλῳ is a cord of flax. It is the tether that kills the bird two sentences later, and the fable puts it in its first line. Birds kept on a string for children to play with are a commonplace of Greek household life.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ οὐχ ὑπομείνας τὴν μετ’ ἀνθρώπων δίαιταν, ὡς πρὸς ὀλίγον ἀδείας ἔτυχε, φυγὼν ἧκεν εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ καλιάν.
sentences.tr: Ho de ouch hypomeinas tēn met’ anthrōpōn diaitan, hōs pros oligon adeias etyche, phygōn hēken eis tēn heautou kalian.
sentences.l: But he, not having endured the life among men, when for a little he met with freedom from fear, having fled came to his own nest.
sentences.i: But the bird would not put up with living among men, and the moment he was left unwatched for a little, he escaped and made for his own nest.
sentences.n: ἄδεια is freedom from fear, and so an unguarded moment; τυγχάνω takes its genitive. ὡς here is temporal, 'when'. πρὸς ὀλίγον, 'for a short while'. δίαιτα once more — one jackdaw fable after another turns on where the bird is to live.

sentences.t: Περιειληθέντος δὲ τοῦ δέσμου τοῖς κλάδοις, ἀναπτῆναι μὴ δυνάμενος, ἐπειδὴ ἀποθνῄσκειν ἔμελλεν, ἔφη πρὸς ἑαυτόν· « Ἀλλ’ ἔγωγε δείλαιος, ὅστις τὴν παρὰ ἀνθρώπων δουλείαν μὴ ὑπομείνας ἔλαθον ἐμαυτὸν καὶ σωτηρίας στερήσας. »
sentences.tr: Perieilēthentos de tou desmou tois kladois, anaptēnai mē dynamenos, epeidē apothnēiskein emellen, ephē pros heauton· « All’ egōge deilaios, hostis tēn para anthrōpōn douleian mē hypomeinas elathon emauton kai sōtērias sterēsas. »
sentences.l: But the tether having been wound about the branches, being unable to fly up, when he was about to die, he said to himself: « But I for my part am a wretch, who, not having endured the slavery at men's hands, escaped my own notice depriving myself of safety as well. »
sentences.i: But the cord got wound about the branches, and unable to fly up, when he was on the point of death he said to himself: « Wretch that I am — because I would not endure slavery at men's hands, I have robbed myself of my safety too, and never knew I was doing it. »
sentences.n: Περιειληθέντος τοῦ δέσμου is a genitive absolute. ἔλαθον ἐμαυτὸν … στερήσας is λανθάνω with a participle in its fullest form: 'I escaped my own notice depriving myself', that is, I did it and never saw myself doing it. στερέω takes the genitive of what is taken away, and σωτηρία here is not rescue but simply staying alive. καί is 'as well' — losing his freedom was the price he meant to pay, and his life went with it.

sentences.t: Οὗτος ὁ λόγος ἁρμόσειεν ἂν ἐπ’ ἐκείνων τῶν ἀνθρώπων οἳ μετρίων ἑαυτοὺς κινδύνων ῥύσασθαι βουλόμενοι ἔλαθον εἰς μείζονα δεινὰ περιπεσόντες.
sentences.tr: Houtos ho logos harmoseien an ep’ ekeinōn tōn anthrōpōn hoi metriōn heautous kindynōn rhysasthai boulomenoi elathon eis meizona deina peripesontes.
sentences.l: This story would fit those men who, wishing to rescue themselves from moderate dangers, fell without noticing it into greater terrors.
sentences.n: The ἁρμόζει formula — 'this story fits…' — here in the potential optative, ἁρμόσειεν ἄν, 'would fit', a shade more guarded, and with ἐπί and the genitive where πρός and the accusative usually stand. ῥύομαι, 'to draw out of danger', takes the genitive of what one is drawn from. ἔλαθον … περιπεσόντες is the same λανθάνω idiom the jackdaw has just used of himself, now turned on the reader.
